data.title: Prosiek – Hrádok, a Púchov culture hillfort above the Prosiecka valley
data.excerpt: A small fort of the Púchov culture on a limestone crag at 823 m above sea level, at the entrance to the Prosiecka valley, was later renewed and used by the Slavs between the 9th and the 12th century. Today it is the only Slavic hilltop settlement known in the Liptov region, and the finds from it range from a La Tène wheel-shaped pendant to Slavic shears and an arrowhead.
data.metaTitle: Prosiek – Hrádok, a Púchov culture hillfort in Liptov
data.metaDescription: A small fort of the Púchov culture, later Slavic (9th–12th century), on a limestone crag at 823 m at the entrance to the Prosiecka valley; discovered in 1891.

keyFacts.label: Discoverer
keyFacts.value: Jozef Mihalik, secondary-school teacher in Liptovský Sv. Mikuláš (1891)

keyFacts.label: Ground plan
keyFacts.value: An irregular elongated shape with the main axis running east–west

keyFacts.label: Fortification
keyFacts.value: A rampart mound on the western slope of the summit plateau, today visible as pronounced terracing

keyFacts.label: Finds
keyFacts.value: Pottery, an iron needle, an awl, a buckle made of bronze wire, an arrowhead, shears and a wheel-shaped bronze pendant of the La Tène period

keyFacts.label: What makes the site unique
keyFacts.value: The only Slavic hilltop settlement in the Liptov region, lying beside an important passage from the Váh region to the north

children.text: A small fort of the Púchov culture, later renewed and used by the Slavs (9th – 12th century), extends over a limestone crag at the entrance to the Prosiecka valley and lies at an elevation of 823 m. On the eastern side the Prosiečanka stream flows around it.

blocks.caption: Plan of the small fort (from M. Furman's book Opevnenia na Liptove, 2016)
blocks.alt: Plan of the small fort (from M. Furman's book Opevnenia na Liptove, 2016)

children.text: The small fort was first discovered in 1891 by Jozef Mihalik, a secondary-school teacher at the grammar school in Liptovský Sv. Mikuláš, who published his observations together with others in a work on the prehistoric hillforts of Liptov, which appeared in the yearbook of the Hungarian Carpathian Society. In the 1970s the small fort was investigated by the prominent Slovak archaeologist Karol Pieta.

In its ground plan the small fort has an irregular elongated shape, with the main axis running east–west. The fortification is probably attested by a rampart mound on the western slope of the summit plateau, which can at present be observed in the form of pronounced terracing. It evidently came into being as early as the period of the Púchov culture. The entrance gateway into the acropolis is situated on the south-eastern side and originally probably had a half-pincer shape.

blocks.caption: Older finds from the small fort (Slavic shears, an arrow, a Púchov culture pendant), published by K. Pieta in AVANS 1993
blocks.alt: Older finds from the small fort (Slavic shears, an arrow, a Púchov culture pendant), published by K. Pieta in AVANS 1993

children.text: During the investigation in the 1970s it was possible to find undiagnostic pottery and several metal objects in the interior of the hillfort. An iron needle 53 mm long, an awl (135 mm) and a buckle with a frame of bronze wire, with the remains of an iron pin. The Slavic horizon of the site undoubtedly includes an arrowhead with long barbs and a twisted shank, 83 mm long, and small iron shears with short narrow blades. Part of a horse bit found here may be of early medieval, but also of La Tène origin. Neither the pottery nor the metal objects allow more detailed dating within the said time spans. In the Liptov Museum in Ružomberok there is a cast bronze pendant of the La Tène period which was discovered at the hillfort and which Mihalik already mentions. It has the form of a wheel with a central, asymmetrically placed hub, six spokes and a grooved surface around the rim. Magical objects in the shape of a wheel (the motif of the sun, of the sun chariot) have been known since the Early Bronze Age.

In the past the Prosiecka valley served as one of the passages from the Váh region towards the north. The Prosiek Hrádok is at present the only Slavic hilltop settlement in the Liptov region. The site is most easily reached from the village of Prosiek in the direction of the western saddle.
